title: Principal Cech totalization compares a quasi-coherent complex with a K-injective resolution
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, r a natural number, f : Fin r → A, and F and J integer-indexed complexes of sheaves of modules on Spec(A). Suppose every F.X n is quasi-coherent, J is K-injective, and i : F → J is a quasi-isomorphism. Then (principalCechFunctor r f).map i [def-sc-principal-open-alternating-total] is a quasi-isomorphism of A-module complexes. No boundedness assumption or quasi-coherence hypothesis on J is imposed.

source.place: Tags 08D2 and 08C2, affine specialization and the finite Cech total comparison with a resolution

proof.text: Use the intersectionwise affine section comparison in the proof of lem-sc-qcoh-complex-alternating-cech-derived-sections: each nonempty principal intersection is affine; restriction of i is a quasi-isomorphism into a K-injective complex, and the terms, differential cokernels, and cohomology of F on that intersection are quasi-coherent and have vanishing higher cohomology. Thus the section map is a quasi-isomorphism, without a vertical boundedness assumption.

Filter the totals by Cech degree. Each graded map is a shifted finite product of the preceding section quasi-isomorphisms. Starting with the zero terminal filtration step, the long exact sequences of the short exact filtration sequences show inductively that each preceding step is a quasi-isomorphism. There are only r rows. The r=0 totals are zero and r=1 has one affine section map.

theorem principalCech_resolution_quasiIso
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → A)
    (F J : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (Spec (.of A)).toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (hF : ∀ n : ℤ, (F.X n).IsQuasicoherent)
    [J.IsKInjective] (i : F ⟶ J) [QuasiIso i] :
    QuasiIso ((principalCechFunctor r f).map i)
